why.sym._main return: expected 'int', said ': With no debug information nothing proves the signedness of a 32-bit return, and the engine spells it unsigned. C has no spelling that declines to say, so whichever is chosen is a claim; `int` is the language's own default and what an unproven 32-bit return usually is. Changing the default moves rendered output across the whole corpus, so it is a decompiler-quality decision rather than an inversion one.
